title: Shut a clamp meter's sprung jaw round the middle of three motor leads, one arm holding it, one on the trigger
instruction: Take the red middle lead's current: shut the clamp meter's jaw round it for 3 s, then put the meter back on its tray.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, 0.8M) test circuits with testing devices and maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00, 1.5M) diagnose equipment faults by clamping a meter round one motor lead. The open jaw must pass between leads 40 mm apart and shut round one alone; unlike board latch, probe or clip tasks, the conductor is enclosed, not gripped.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. STARTER, bolted down, de-energised: light grey steel backplate 30 wide x 46 tall x 0.6, front face at x 39; black contactor 6 x 14 x 8 cm, x 33 to 39, y -7 to 7, 36 to 44 up; mid grey terminal strip 7 x 14 x 6 cm, x 32 to 39, on the table. Three stiff 2 AWG THHN copper motor leads, 1.05 cm over the insulation, vertical at x 34, from the strip (6 up) to the contactor (36 up): T1 black at y +4, T2 red at y 0, T3 blue at y -4. TRAY: dark grey ABS, 24 x 9 x 0.6 cm, centre x 25, y -15. CLAMP METER, 240 g, loose, lying on the tray along x, jaw toward the leads, jaw window centre at x 33.7, y -15: AC/DC Hall-effect clamp meter on its DC A range; safety yellow ABS body 4.0 cm thick, handle 6.6 cm wide x 11.5 long, neck 4.6 wide x 5.6 long, 21.5 cm overall; black jaw ring with a 2.6 cm window, 3.9 cm across, 2.4 cm tall, one half fixed, the right half hinged at its base and sprung shut (0.15 N m/rad); black trigger lever on the neck's right side, standing 2.2 cm out with the jaw shut; squeezed flush against the neck (3.3 N) it opens the tips 2.2 cm.
scoring: Whole run; top camera plus a fixed close camera on the display and jaw. Shut: jaw tips closed (hinge 0.05 rad or less; photo: tips touching). In: window centre within 9 mm of a lead's axis, on its free run 9 to 33 cm up, window axis within 20 deg of the lead. Reading: shut and In on red T2, no finger within 2 cm of the trigger, meter moving under 5 mm and 3 deg, for 3.0 s unbroken; in a real trial the display must also read 4.5 to 5.5 A in that video. 0 if the jaw was ever shut and In on T1 or T3, the meter ever fell (0.4 m/s or more downward), or a gripper is within 3 cm of the meter at the end. Else 1.0: reading, then the meter flat on its tray (centre within 2 cm of its start, resting, tilt 10 deg or less, yaw 20 deg or less), jaw shut, still 1 s. 0.6: reading, meter left anywhere else. 0.3: T2 was In with the jaw open 0.3 rad or more at some time. Else 0.
reset_notes: Lay the meter on its tray outline, jaw shut, toward the leads. Zero the DC A range with the jaw empty. Panel de-energised: a bench supply limited to 5 A at 12 V or less feeds T2; the lead ends are joined at the motor end so 2.5 A returns on each of T1 and T3.
fidelity: Real sizes. Leads are fixed rigid rods, as stiff 2 AWG is under light contact. Trigger and moving jaw half are one rigid bell crank on a linear spring (no preload, no hold); its lever passes through the neck where a real one has a slot. Uniform mass plus a battery block in the handle; no iron core. No display or circuit is simulated. The sim scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a meter still held scores 0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (left arm folded back, right arm moved beside the meter without clamping); demo: 1.0 (carried meter to red lead, clamped it, returned it to tray, backed away)
